description: A detailed study of subject-verb and pronoun-antecedent agreement, covering singular and plural subjects, collective nouns, indefinite pronouns, compound subjects, special nouns, and common concord errors.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: The teacher and the students _____ ready for the examination.
mcq.explanation: Two subjects joined by 'and' form a plural compound subject, so the plural verb 'are' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: Each of the boys _____ a clean uniform.
mcq.explanation: 'Each' is a singular indefinite pronoun and always takes a singular verb, so 'has' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: Neither the manager nor the workers _____ satisfied with the plan.
mcq.explanation: With 'neither...nor', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Workers' is plural, so 'are' is correct (the proximity rule).

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: The news about the floods _____ very disturbing.
mcq.explanation: 'News' is plural in form but singular in meaning, so it takes a singular verb, 'is'.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: Mathematics _____ my favourite subject.
mcq.explanation: Though it ends in '-s', 'mathematics' is treated as a singular noun, so the singular verb 'is' is used.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: There _____ many reasons for his failure.
mcq.explanation: In 'there is/there are' sentences, the verb agrees with the noun that follows. 'Reasons' is plural, so 'are' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: The box of pens _____ on the table.
mcq.explanation: The true subject is 'box' (singular); 'of pens' is a phrase separating the subject from the verb, so the singular 'is' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: The committee _____ divided in their opinions.
mcq.explanation: A collective noun takes a plural verb when its members are thought of as acting individually. 'Divided in their opinions' shows individual action, so 'are' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: Twenty kilometres _____ a long distance to walk.
mcq.explanation: An amount or measurement treated as a single unit takes a singular verb, so 'is' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct pronoun: Every student must bring _____ own textbook.
mcq.explanation: 'Every student' is singular, so the pronoun must be singular. In formal NECTA English, 'his or her' agrees correctly with the singular antecedent.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: Bread and butter _____ a common breakfast in many homes.
mcq.explanation: 'Bread and butter' is a single idea (one dish), so it is treated as singular and takes 'is'.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: None of the water _____ been wasted.
mcq.explanation: 'None' takes a singular verb when it refers to an uncountable noun like 'water', so 'has' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: Either my brother or my sisters _____ going to help me.
mcq.explanation: With 'either...or', the verb agrees with the nearer subject. 'Sisters' is plural, so 'are' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: Furniture in the new offices _____ been bought.
mcq.explanation: 'Furniture' is an uncountable noun and takes a singular verb, so 'has' is correct.

mcq.questionText: Choose the correct verb: Great Expectations _____ written by Charles Dickens.
mcq.explanation: A title of a single book is treated as singular even when it looks plural, so 'was' is correct.

fib.questionText: Everybody in the class _____ (was/were) present yesterday.
fib.explanation: 'Everybody' is a singular indefinite pronoun, so it takes the singular verb 'was'.
'Scissors' is a noun that is always plural and takes a plural verb, 'are'.
'Neither' is singular and takes a singular verb, so 'is' is correct.

fib.questionText: The number of candidates _____ (has/have) increased this year.
fib.explanation: 'The number of' is treated as a singular subject, so it takes 'has'.

fib.questionText: Physics _____ (is/are) a difficult but interesting subject.
fib.explanation: 'Physics' is plural in form but singular in meaning, so it takes 'is'.

fib.questionText: There _____ (was/were) a cat and three dogs in the yard.
fib.explanation: A compound subject joined by 'and' ('a cat and three dogs') is plural, so the plural verb 'were' is used: 'There were a cat and three dogs in the yard.'

fib.questionText: The students, together with their teacher, _____ (is/are) on a trip.
fib.explanation: The phrase 'together with their teacher' does not change the subject. The subject 'students' is plural, so 'are' is correct.

fib.questionText: One of my friends _____ (live/lives) in Dodoma.
fib.explanation: The subject is 'one' (singular); 'of my friends' is a phrase. The singular verb 'lives' is correct.

fib.questionText: Money _____ (is/are) not the only thing that brings happiness.
fib.explanation: 'Money' is an uncountable noun and takes the singular verb 'is'.

fib.questionText: Each boy and each girl _____ (was/were) given a prize.
fib.explanation: When 'each' precedes singular subjects joined by 'and', the verb is singular, so 'was' is correct.

tf.questionText: The sentence 'The dogs barks loudly at night' is grammatically correct.
tf.explanation: The subject 'dogs' is plural and needs the plural verb 'bark', not 'barks'.

tf.questionText: The indefinite pronoun 'everyone' takes a singular verb.
tf.explanation: 'Everyone' is singular, so it correctly takes a singular verb, as in 'Everyone is here.'

tf.questionText: In 'there is/there are' sentences, the verb agrees with the noun that follows it.
tf.explanation: The verb in such sentences agrees with the real subject placed after it, for example 'There are many books.'

tf.questionText: The word 'news' takes a plural verb because it ends in '-s'.
tf.explanation: Although 'news' ends in '-s', it is singular in meaning and takes a singular verb, as in 'The news is good.'

tf.questionText: When two singular subjects are joined by 'and', they normally take a plural verb.
tf.explanation: Subjects joined by 'and' usually form a plural compound subject, as in 'Tom and Jane are friends.'

tf.questionText: With 'neither...nor', the verb always agrees with the first subject.
tf.explanation: The verb agrees with the nearer (second) subject under the proximity rule, not the first.

tf.questionText: The sentence 'Each of the students have a desk' is correct.
tf.explanation: 'Each' is singular, so the correct verb is 'has': 'Each of the students has a desk.'

tf.questionText: Uncountable nouns such as 'furniture' and 'information' take singular verbs.
tf.explanation: Uncountable nouns are treated as singular, as in 'The information is useful.'

tf.questionText: The sentence 'Mathematics are easy for her' is grammatically correct.
tf.explanation: 'Mathematics' is singular in meaning, so the correct verb is 'is': 'Mathematics is easy for her.'

tf.questionText: A pronoun must agree in number with the antecedent it refers to.
tf.explanation: Pronoun-antecedent agreement requires a singular pronoun for a singular antecedent and a plural pronoun for a plural one.

summary.questionText: In one sentence, state the basic rule of subject-verb agreement (concord).
summary.correctAnswer: A singular subject takes a singular verb and a plural subject takes a plural verb.
summary.explanation: This is the fundamental rule of concord on which all other rules build.

summary.questionText: Briefly explain the proximity rule used with 'or' and 'nor'.
summary.correctAnswer: When subjects are joined by 'or' or 'nor', the verb agrees with the subject nearer to it.
summary.explanation: The proximity rule lets the closer subject determine whether the verb is singular or plural.

summary.questionText: Explain in one sentence how verbs agree with collective nouns.
summary.correctAnswer: A collective noun takes a singular verb when the group acts as one unit and a plural verb when its members act individually.
summary.explanation: Concord with collective nouns depends on whether the group is seen as a whole or as separate members.

summary.questionText: State the agreement rule for indefinite pronouns such as 'each', 'everyone' and 'neither'.
summary.correctAnswer: Indefinite pronouns like each, everyone and neither are singular and take singular verbs.
summary.explanation: These pronouns refer to one item or person at a time, so they require singular verbs.

summary.questionText: Explain why nouns like 'news' and 'physics' take singular verbs.
summary.correctAnswer: Although they are plural in form, they are singular in meaning, so they take singular verbs.
summary.explanation: Such nouns end in '-s' but name a single subject or idea, so concord treats them as singular.

summary.questionText: Describe how the verb agrees in 'there is' and 'there are' sentences.
summary.correctAnswer: The verb agrees with the noun that follows it, being singular for a singular noun and plural for a plural noun.
summary.explanation: In these structures the real subject comes after the verb and controls its number.

summary.questionText: Explain how a phrase between the subject and verb affects agreement.
summary.correctAnswer: A phrase separating the subject from the verb does not change the number of the subject, which still controls the verb.
summary.explanation: Phrases like 'of the boys' or 'together with' must be ignored when choosing the verb.

summary.questionText: State the agreement rule for uncountable nouns.
summary.explanation: Nouns such as water, furniture and information cannot be counted and are treated as singular.

summary.questionText: Explain how titles of books and amounts of money or distance agree with verbs.
summary.correctAnswer: Titles of single works and amounts treated as one unit take singular verbs.
summary.explanation: Even when they look plural, a single title or a single sum or measurement is treated as singular.

summary.questionText: State the rule of pronoun-antecedent agreement in one sentence.
summary.correctAnswer: A pronoun must agree with its antecedent in number, person and gender.
summary.explanation: Correct concord requires the pronoun to match the noun it refers back to.

hoq.questionText: Identify the sentence that uses concord CORRECTLY.

options.text: The list of items are on the notice board.
Neither the head teacher nor the prefects was informed.
Each of the candidates has signed the register.
Mathematics are taught by Mr. Juma.

hoq.explanation: Option (c) is correct because 'each' is singular and takes 'has'. (a) should be 'is' (subject 'list'), (b) should be 'were' (proximity to plural 'prefects'), and (d) should be 'is' (singular 'mathematics').

hoq.questionText: Choose the option that correctly rewrites this faulty sentence: 'The team are playing well, and it have won every match.'

options.text: The team is playing well, and it has won every match.
The team are playing well, and they has won every match.
The team is playing well, and they have won every match.
The team are playing well, and it have won every match.

hoq.explanation: When the team acts as one unit, it takes a singular verb and the singular pronoun 'it'. Option (a) keeps both the verb and pronoun singular and consistent, so it is correct.

hoq.questionText: Which sentence shows correct agreement between the verb and a subject separated from it by a phrase?

options.text: The quality of the roads have improved greatly.
A bunch of bananas were hanging on the wall.
The collection of old coins are very valuable.
The basket of fruits is in the kitchen.

hoq.explanation: In (d) the true subject is 'basket' (singular), so 'is' is correct. In (a), (b) and (c) the singular head nouns 'quality', 'bunch' and 'collection' require 'has', 'was' and 'is' respectively.
